items.text: India's foreign ministry condemned an attack on the Panama-flagged LPG tanker Tara Gas in the Strait of Hormuz, saying one of its 24 Indian crew is missing and two are injured; a second tanker was hit north of Oman's Khasab. The [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] says another tanker struck a mine. A US official told Reuters US aircraft hit an IRGC launch site on Qeshm, while another official reported no damage; the accounts conflict.
items.notes: Indian minister Sonowal separately said all crew were safe; MEA figures used. Qeshm strike unconfirmed and disputed.

items.text: The [[p:Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention|Africa CDC]] says DR Congo's Bundibugyo [[e:Ebola outbreak|2026 Ebola epidemic]] is still not under control: over 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths in eight of 26 provinces since 15 May, making it the second-largest on record. Over 80% of new cases come from outside known contact lists, and only $1.3bn of $2.9bn pledged has been released.
items.notes: Figures from DRC government data cited by Africa CDC.

items.text: AFP puts [[p:Houthis|Houthi]] forces about 60 km northwest of Aden after they took al-Maqatirah and al-Madaribah districts; Reuters places them at Khor Omaira, about 100 km west. Saudi Arabia named Gen. Fayyad al-Ruwaili as new Joint Forces commander, and the Houthis say they launched drones at the East-West pipeline.
items.notes: AFP and Reuters distance estimates differ.

items.text: [[p:Xi Jinping]] met [[p:Donald Trump]] at the foot of the stairs at Shenzhen airport on 18 Nov, an unusual courtesy, with honour guards and a military flypast. A bilateral summit on trade and tech export controls follows on 19 Nov, then the first-ever US–China–Russia leaders' meeting with [[p:Vladimir Putin]], expected to cover Ukraine and nuclear arms control. Taiwan is represented at [[e:APEC China 2026]] by Acer founder Stan Shih.
items.notes: SBS English text is machine-translated from Korean.

items.text: ASEAN and China failed to conclude a [[e:South China Sea code of conduct|Code of Conduct in the South China Sea]] in Manila despite tentative agreement on about 80% of the draft; whether it is legally binding remains unresolved. Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro hopes Singapore, chair from 2027, finishes it. ASEAN also extended its ban on [[p:Min Aung Hlaing]] attending summits; Myanmar may send only career diplomats.

At the ASEAN–US special summit, [[p:Bongbong Marcos|Marcos]] said leaders adopted principles and a work plan against online scams. Trump and Thai PM [[p:Anutin Charnvirakul]] signed a joint trade statement; Trump says Thailand will drop tariffs on US exports and buy $2.6bn of US farm goods, with a formal deal due 'in the coming weeks'.
items.notes: Draft chair statement marked partnership statement adoption "TBC" (Asia Media Centre).

items.text: The first in-person [[p:Quad|Quadrilateral Security Dialogue]] leaders' summit since 2024 announced five outcomes, including [[e:Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration]] with a first joint P-8/P-3C patrol-aircraft exercise in 2027, a cable-resilience partnership and a business forum in Mumbai. Leaders voiced 'grave concerns' about economic coercion 'including through arbitrary export restrictions' and pledged secure critical-mineral supply chains, without naming China.

President [[p:Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh]] announced his resignation after a rival [[p:Mongolian People's Party]] faction figure, ex-Ulaanbaatar mayor Nyambaatar Khishgee, accused him of taking $25m over a 2019 no-tender railway contract. He denies wrongdoing and says he will cooperate with investigators. The [[p:State Great Khural]] must accept the resignation, expected this week; its speaker would then be interim president.
items.notes: link2 Bloomberg is paywalled. Bodi International denies paying bribes.

items.text: Vice President [[p:Gibran Rakabuming Raka]], son of ex-president [[p:Joko Widodo]], resigned weeks after the Supreme Court voided the school-equivalency certificate he used to run in 2024; he says the two are unrelated. Under the constitution the [[p:People's Consultative Assembly]] must elect a replacement from two candidates named by [[p:Prabowo Subianto]] within 60 days. The rupiah hit a record low that day.

Police chief Suyudi Ario Seto told parliament that former police chief [[p:Listyo Sigit Prabowo]], arrested with three generals earlier in November, was the 'end user' of illegal wiretaps on [[p:Prabowo Subianto|President Prabowo]] and journalists. Police are pursuing treason charges but say they still need evidence of a plot to overthrow the government.
items.notes: Police allegations; not tested in court.

items.text: The [[p:Barisan Nasional]]–[[p:Perikatan Nasional]] pact won 24 of 28 seats in the [[e:2026 Malacca state election]]; [[p:Pakatan Harapan]] kept only four DAP seats. The vote was framed as a test of the court ruling letting [[p:Najib Razak]] serve his sentence under house arrest, after which DAP leader [[p:Anthony Loke]] quit as transport minister; [[p:Anwar Ibrahim]] has not accepted the resignation. BN is pushing for an early general election.

Two suspected Russian military aircraft entered Japanese airspace near Okinoshima for about three minutes each before flying through the Tsushima Strait and between Yonaguni and Taiwan; Japan scrambled fighters and protested, calling it a 'grave infringement'. Seoul scrambled jets as Russian aircraft crossed its air-defence zone but reported no airspace violation.

[[p:Sanae Takaichi]] attends APEC in her first China visit since the [[e:2025–2026 China–Japan diplomatic crisis|row over her Taiwan remarks]], but diplomatic sources tell Kyodo formal talks with Xi are unlikely. In Manila she met South Korea's [[p:Lee Jae Myung]], who called for renewed inter-Korean dialogue at the East Asia Summit and will visit Japan in January.

Trump says he might meet [[p:Kim Jong Un]] in China and that it is 'up to' Xi; Beijing's foreign ministry says it has 'no information'. State media showed Kim touring Samjiyon near the Chinese border on 15–16 Nov, and a Seoul government think-tank analyst sees 'no signs' of summit preparations.

The [[p:Bureau of Industry and Security]] issued a rule closing the loophole that let Chinese firms use advanced US AI chips remotely through overseas data centres. It follows [[p:Jensen Huang]]'s exit as Nvidia CEO amid reports linking him to Alice Huang, ex-chief of Singapore data-centre firm Megaspeed, which is under US criminal investigation over chip access for Chinese clients.
items.notes: Huang relationship reports not verified by NPR. No Chinese reaction reported yet.

items.text: After meeting [[p:Mark Carney]] in Shenzhen, Beijing will cut tariffs on about C$400m of Canadian exports, including pork and seafood; Ottawa extends steel and aluminium exemptions for two years and adds 32 items. It builds on January's deal cutting Canada's EV tariff from 100% to 6.1%.
October data missed forecasts: industrial output rose 4.8% year on year and retail sales just 0.4%, while fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in January–October, the National Bureau of Statistics said.

A military airstrike on the Byar La displacement camp in Ponnagyun, northeast of Sittwe, killed 12 people including a five-year-old and injured 18, a local rescue foundation says; the junta did not comment. The [[p:Arakan Army]] holds Ponnagyun as the junta tries to push out from Sittwe.
items.notes: BNI reported at least eight dead; tolls differ.

items.text: The Philippine military counted 19 Chinese navy and coast guard ships at Scarborough, Second Thomas and Sabina shoals and near Thitu (Pag-asa) on 9–16 Nov, down from 29 the week before.

Thailand objected to Cambodia's push to cite over 20,000 displaced people in an ASEAN parliamentary statement, and [[p:Anutin Charnvirakul|Anutin]] urged Phnom Penh to keep the border dispute out of international forums after [[p:Hun Manet]] raised it at the Francophonie summit.
